question: How much of frozen Book A's result survives perpetual funding and KuCoin contract sizes?
why: simulate_book_a never charged funding although Book A holds long perpetuals; the intended venue (KuCoin) has integer contract sizes and, over 2026-09-27..10-27, charged longs about 1.6x the Binance funding on the same six markets.
subject: BOOK_A_ALT_RM + BOOK_A_RISK_DEFAULT, stress cost (12 bps one-way turnover), unchanged rules

variants.V0_frozen: as frozen: no funding, fractional quantities, $250
variants.V2_kucoin_funding: V0 + Binance funding x1.6 (30-day KuCoin/Binance ratio; sensitivity, not a measured history)
variants.V3_kucoin_250: V2 + KuCoin contract steps (SOL 0.1, XRP 10, DOGE 100, BNB 0.01, ETH 0.01, BTC 0.001), $250

book_b_check: Distribution of Book B BTC position sizes vs the 0.001 BTC contract (rounding error per trade).
decision_use: V3 replaces V0 as the realistic expectation for a KuCoin canary; if V3 is <= 0 in the OOS window or in two of three historical windows, Book A is not canary-ready at $250.
disclosure: Retrospective correction of an existing frozen benchmark; parameters unchanged.
